hints.content:
There are two ways we slice the cube diagonal to one of its faces.

One way is to use a plane parallel to one of the edges:



[[☃ image 2]]

Another way is to use a plane that *isn't* parallel to any of the edges:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A cube with a rectangle through it that represents the cross-section. The rectangle is at an angle so that it is not parallel to any side. The rectangle moves through the entire cube showing the following possible cross-sections: a triangle, a parallelogram, and a pentagon.

A cube with a rectangle through it that represents the cross-section. The rectangle is at an angle so that it is parallel to an edge of the cube. The rectangle moves through the entire cube showing every possible cross-section. It cross-sections include a rectangle and a square.

hints.content:
Slicing the cube the first way, we always create a **rectangle**.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A cube with a rectangle through it that represents the cross-section. The rectangle is at an angle so that it is parallel to an edge of the cube. The rectangle moves through the entire cube showing every possible cross-section. It cross-sections include a rectangle and a square.

hints.content:
Slicing the cube the other way, we can get a triangle.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A cube with a rectangle through it that represents the cross-section. The rectangle is at an angle so that it is not parallel to any side. The rectangle moves through the entire cube showing every possible cross-section. It cross-sections include a triangle, a parallelogram, a pentagon, and a hexagon.

hints.content:
These are the cross-sections we could create by slicing the cube diagonal to one of its faces:

- Triangle
- Rectangle

*Note:* There are other possible cross-sections which were not answer choices.

question.content:
Here is a cube:



[[☃ image 1]]

**What two of the following shapes of cross-sections could we create by slicing the cube *diagonal* to one of its faces?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.content: Shape with two edges, one straight and one curved
